terra.problem: Calling the other three kings rich adds a detail the text does not give.
The explanation is generic and offers little of Papa Dorin's voice.
The verse identifies him as one of the king of the South's commanders, so saying it has him serving nobody overstates the text.
The commander himself grows stronger, not one of his strengths. The text also does not say what happens to his army.
The joke compares sealing a cookie box with sealing an agreement, but those are different actions.
The verse says the king marches out; it does not establish that nobody is hiding.
This is a flat restatement without Papa Dorin's personality.
Saying nobody gets a throne goes beyond what the verse states.
The verse does not establish that no kingdom gets split.
The text does not say his reign lasts only a few days.
No crown, no parade and slipping in a side door add details about how he takes the kingdom that the text does not give.
The verse says royal honors will not be given to him, not that nobody hands him anything.
The line about the happiest person at the party adds an unmarked guess about someone's feeling.
The text does not establish that the South gets nothing from him.
The text does not say the South has the biggest army.
The explanation is generic and repeats the reason without adding Papa Dorin's voice.
The verse says the flattery corrupts; it does not state that its aim is to make people follow him.
